input.title: Tunde Adebayo — UCL Computer Science MSc personal statement
input.body:
I am applying to the UCL Computer Science MSc to develop my preparation for applied research in artificial intelligence and machine learning. My background is a BEng in Electrical and Electronic Engineering from Covenant University, completed in 2023, with a cumulative GPA of 3.72/4.00. My transcript includes Signals and Systems, Probability and Statistics, Linear Algebra, Control Systems, Digital Signal Processing, and Data Structures.

Since January 2024 I have worked as a machine-learning engineer at GridSense Africa, where I have built load-forecasting pipelines and anomaly-detection prototypes for distribution networks. My technical work uses Python, PyTorch, embedded C, signal processing, and MLOps. My final-year project focused on edge inference for low-cost power-quality sensors, which developed my interest in applying computational methods to engineering and infrastructure problems.

I am also the author of the manuscript “Self-supervised event detection for weak distribution grids,” submitted to IEEE Transactions on Smart Grid on 4 May 2026; no decision has been received. This manuscript status is reported as submitted, not accepted or published.

The MSc would help me strengthen my computer-science foundations and develop more rigorous approaches to machine learning, with the goal of progressing toward applied research and engineering work in AI. I can self-fund tuition up to £18,000 and would need financial support above that amount. I have no disciplinary history.

I recognise that my transcript does not contain a course titled Machine Learning. I therefore present my preparation through my documented programming, data, signal-processing, engineering, and machine-learning experience rather than claiming a named prerequisite course.
